title: Demaine et al. Open Question on Token Sliding for Interval and Chordal Graphs
statement_text: Can determining whether two independent sets are in the same connected component of $TS_k(G)$ be decided in polynomial time for interval graphs, and more generally for chordal graphs?
context_text: Demaine et al. [8] asked whether the Token Sliding reconfiguration problem is polynomial time solvable on interval graphs and more generally in chordal graphs. Yamada and Uehara [21] had previously shown that a polynomial time transformation can be found in proper interval graphs.
paper_contribution: Proves that the connectivity of $TS_k(G)$ can be decided in polynomial time when $G$ is an interval graph (Theorems 2 and 3), fully answering the interval graph case; also shows the problem is co-NP-hard and co-W[2]-hard parameterized by the size of the independent set for split graphs, a subclass of chordal graphs (Theorem 1).

title: Question 1
statement_text: For any integers $k$, $D$, for any chordal graph $G$ of clique-tree degree at most $D$, can the connectivity of $TS_k(G)$ be decided in polynomial time?
context_text: For a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the $k$-token-sliding reconfiguration graph $TS_k(G)$ has the independent sets of size $k$ of $G$ as vertices, two independent sets $I,J$ being adjacent if $J\setminus I=\{u\}$, $I\setminus J=\{v\}$ and $uv$ is an edge of $G$ (a token is slid along an edge while the token set stays independent). A clique tree of a chordal graph $G$ is a tree whose nodes are the maximal cliques of $G$ such that, for every vertex $v$, the cliques containing $v$ induce a subtree (every chordal graph has one; interval graphs are exactly the chordal graphs admitting a clique tree that is a path). The clique-tree degree of a chordal graph $G$ is the smallest maximum degree of a clique tree of $G$. Deciding whether two independent sets are in the same component of $TS_k(G)$ is PSPACE-complete even for planar graphs (Hearn and Demaine), and Demaine et al. asked about interval and chordal graphs. The authors prove that the connectivity of $TS_k(G)$ (and whether two given independent sets are in the same component) can be decided in polynomial time for interval graphs, while deciding whether $TS_k(G)$ is connected is co-NP-hard, and co-W[2]-hard parameterized by $k$, for split graphs. In light of these two results they ask whether bounding the clique-tree degree restores tractability.
